definitions.explanation: A simple rice porridge made with seven spring herbs, traditionally eaten on January 7th to pray for good health throughout the year and to rest the stomach after New Year's feasting.

examples.japanese: ⟦{一月|いちがつ}→一月：00631_ichigatsu⟧⟦{七日|なのか}→七日：02927_nanoka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{七草粥|ななくさがゆ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: We eat seven-herb porridge on January 7th.

examples.japanese: {七草粥|ななくさがゆ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{胃|い}→胃：01706_i⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{優|やさ}しい⟦{料理|りょうり}→料理：01523_ryouri⟧だ。
examples.english: Seven-herb porridge is a dish that's gentle on the stomach.

examples.japanese: ⟦{正月|しょうがつ}→正月：01433_shougatsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{食|た}べ{過|す}ぎた→食べ過ぎる：21686_tabesugiru⟧⟦{後|あと}→後：09580_ato⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{七草粥|ななくさがゆ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べて→食べる：00396_taberu⟧⟦{体|からだ}→体：00784_karada⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{休|やす}める→休める：02437_yasumeru⟧。
examples.english: After overeating during New Year's, we eat seven-herb porridge to give our bodies a rest.

notes:
A traditional Japanese dish eaten on January 7th ({人日|じんじつ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{節句|せっく}→節句：26925_sekku⟧). The seven herbs (⟦{春|はる}の{七草|ななくさ}→春の七草：26510_harunonanakusa⟧) are: せり (water dropwort), なずな (shepherd's purse), ごぎょう (cudweed), はこべら (chickweed), ほとけのざ (henbit), すずな (turnip), and すずしろ (daikon radish). Supermarkets sell pre-packaged ⟦{七草|ななくさ}→七草：11190_nanakusa⟧⟦セット→セット：03853_setto⟧ (seven-herb sets) in early January.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {七草粥|ななくさがゆ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧: to eat seven-herb porridge
- {七草粥|ななくさがゆ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧: to make seven-herb porridge
- ⟦{春|はる}の{七草|ななくさ}→春の七草：26510_harunonanakusa⟧: the seven spring herbs

CULTURAL NOTE:
The custom has roots in ancient Chinese tradition and was adopted in Japan during the Heian period. The porridge is intentionally bland — it serves as a reset for the digestive system after rich New Year foods ({御節料理|おせちりょうり}). It is also associated with prayers for good health ({無病息災|むびょうそくさい}).
